item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. There is some narrow positive evidence of humanitarian/protection programs for Rohingya, women, transgender people, sex workers, and indigenous women, but it is largely partner-led and not strong evidence of Hasina protecting political equality. The stronger 2024 record points the other way: repression of opposition, internet shutdowns, and failures to protect minorities and indigenous communities from violence.

- **UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report** — UNFPA Bangladesh — 2024 — https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024 — Claim: UNFPA says it delivered targeted services to persons with disabilities, transgender individuals, sex workers, indigenous communities, and adolescents in crisis-affected areas; 3,089 mothers including 592 indigenous women accessed family planning, and 300+ transgender people and 97 sex workers received tailored services. This is the best positive evidence I found, but it is humanitarian service delivery rather than a demonstrated political-equality strategy by Hasina. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`

- **UNFPA Bangladesh Transparency Portal** — UNFPA — 2024 — https://www.unfpa.org/data/transparency-portal/unfpa-bangladesh — Claim: UNFPA reports that Bangladesh supported gender-inclusive, human-rights-oriented reproductive health services and that 73% of Upazila Health Complexes in priority districts provided midwifery-led services, with 154,000 vaginal deliveries and 4,300 GBV-service referrals. Positive, but still partner-led and not strong proof of Hasina personally protecting political equality. `4B.7`, `3B.7`

- **UN and partners seek $852.4m to support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts** — UNHCR — March 13, 2024 — https://www.unhcr.org/news/press-releases/un-and-partners-seek-852-4m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts — Claim: the 2024 Joint Response Plan was launched under Bangladeshi authorities and aimed to protect and assist Rohingya refugees and host communities. This is real protection infrastructure, but it is external-partner driven and does not show Hasina broadening political equality. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`

- **Seven years of crisis for Rohingya refugees** — UNHCR / UN in Bangladesh — August 30, 2024 — https://bangladesh.un.org/en/277640-seven-years-crisis-rohingya-refugees — Claim: UNHCR says Bangladesh’s support has been critical in meeting Rohingya basic needs and protection, but new security concerns and funding uncertainty were undermining assistance. This supports a narrow humanitarian-positive reading, not a strong political-equality one. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`

- **Vandalism, Attacks Follow Bangladesh Prime Minister’s Exit** — Human Rights Watch — August 8, 2024 — https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/08/vandalism-attacks-follow-bangladesh-prime-ministers-exit — Claim: after Hasina’s departure, HRW reported attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities, with homes and temples torched. This shows 2024 did not end with minorities protected against reprisals. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`

- **World Report 2025: Bangladesh** — Human Rights Watch — 2025 — https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/bangladesh — Claim: HRW says the January 2024 election was not inclusive, then the July crackdown killed nearly 1,000 people including over 100 children, followed by reprisals and attacks on minorities after Hasina’s ouster. Retrospectively, this is strong evidence that political equality for excluded groups worsened rather than improved in 2024. `4B.7`, `4B.1`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- **Fears grip ethnic minorities after deadly violence in Bangladesh** — Reuters — September 21, 2024 — https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/fears-grip-ethnic-minorities-after-deadly-violence-in-bangladesh-3626672 — Claim: Reuters reported ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts were living in fear after clashes, with homes and businesses burned and families displaced despite heavy patrols. This is direct evidence that opposition regions and minorities were not securely protected in 2024. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`

- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** — Freedom House — 2024 — https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024 — Claim: Freedom House says the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the BNP and critical media, used state resources coercively, and faced a widely questioned Election Commission independence. This is evidence against political equality for opposition viewpoints and regions. `4B.7`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`

- **Bangladesh repression, security force abuses discredit elections** — Human Rights Watch — January 11, 2024 — https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections — Claim: HRW says authorities arrested critics and opposition members, using repression and violence before the January election. This is direct evidence against equal treatment of unpopular viewpoints and opposition forces. `4B.7`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** — Reuters — July 20, 2024 — https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/ — Claim: Reuters described soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns during the crackdown. That is evidence against protecting political equality for protesters, students, and dissenting regions. `4B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.6`

- **Bangladesh’s crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says** — UN/OHCHR — July 26, 2024 — https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights — Claim: the UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This corroborates a coercive environment that did not protect minorities, women, or unpopular viewpoints. `4B.7`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.6`

**Search Gap**
I did not find reliable evidence that Hasina used 2024 state power to meaningfully advance political equality for minorities, women, excluded groups, opposition regions, or unpopular viewpoints. The best positives are humanitarian and service-delivery programs, mostly via UN partners, while the stronger evidence is repression, coercive shutdowns, and minority vulnerability.
